From 9f1168cf263aab0474300f7118107f8ef73e7423 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2021 15:20:45 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] PCI: controller: PCI_IXP4XX should depend on ARCH_IXP4XX

The Intel IXP4xx PCI controller is only present on Intel IXP4xx
XScale-based network processor SoCs.

Add a dependency on ARCH_IXP4XX, to prevent asking the user about this
driver when configuring a kernel without support for the XScale
processor family.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/6a88e55fe58fc280f4ff1ca83c154e4895b6dcbf.1624972789.git.geert+renesas@glider.be
Fixes: f7821b4934584824 ("PCI: ixp4xx: Add a new driver for IXP4xx")
Signed-off-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
[lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com: commit log]
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Pieralisi <lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

diff --git a/drivers/pci/controller/Kconfig b/drivers/pci/controller/Kconfig
index 5e1e3796efa4..326f7d13024f 100644
--- a/drivers/pci/controller/Kconfig
+++ b/drivers/pci/controller/Kconfig
@@ -40,6 +40,7 @@ config PCI_FTPCI100
 config PCI_IXP4XX
 	bool "Intel IXP4xx PCI controller"
 	depends on ARM && OF
+	depends on ARCH_IXP4XX || COMPILE_TEST
 	default ARCH_IXP4XX
 	help
 	  Say Y here if you want support for the PCI host controller found
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/pci/controller/Kconfig`**
   - Added a new dependency for the `PCI_IXP4XX` configuration option:
     - `depends on ARCH_IXP4XX || COMPILE_TEST`
   - This change ensures that the Intel IXP4xx PCI controller driver is only presented as an option when the architecture is set to IXP4XX or when compiling for testing purposes.

### Relationships
- The modification establishes a clear relationship between the PCI controller driver and the architecture it is intended for. By adding the dependency on `ARCH_IXP4XX`, the patch prevents the configuration of the PCI IXP4XX driver in environments that do not support the Intel IXP4xx architecture, thereby avoiding potential misconfigurations and user confusion. This change is a direct response to the need for architecture-specific driver support, as indicated in the commit message and the linked discussion.

PCI: controller: PCI_IXP4XX should depend on ARCH_IXP4XX

XScale-based network processor SoCs.

Add a dependency on ARCH_IXP4XX, to prevent asking the user about this
driver when configuring a kernel without support for the XScale
processor family.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/6a88e55fe58fc280f4ff1ca83c154e4895b6dcbf.1624972789.git.geert+renesas@glider.be
Fixes: f7821b4934584824 ("PCI: ixp4xx: Add a new driver for IXP4xx")
Signed-off-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
[lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com: commit log]
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Pieralisi <lorenzo.pieralisi@arm.com>
Reviewed-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the lack of a proper dependency check for the `PCI_IXP4XX` driver in the kernel configuration, which could lead to the driver being presented as an option even when the architecture (ARCH_IXP4XX) is not supported, potentially causing misconfigurations and user confusion during kernel setup.

Here is the patch:
 	bool "Intel IXP4xx PCI controller"
 	depends on ARM && OF
+	depends on ARCH_IXP4XX || COMPILE_TEST
 	default ARCH_IXP4XX
 	help

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
bool "Intel IXP4xx PCI controller"
depends on ARM && OF
```
Reason:
The `PCI_IXP4XX` driver is presented as an option without a proper dependency check for `ARCH_IXP4XX`. This means that users could see this driver in the configuration menu even if their architecture does not support it, leading to potential misconfigurations.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
depends on ARCH_IXP4XX || COMPILE_TEST
```
Reason:
By adding the dependency on `ARCH_IXP4XX`, the driver will only be presented as an option when the architecture is supported, preventing user confusion and ensuring that the driver is only available in appropriate configurations.
